  • As , the second point slides back along the curve to the first, and the secant direction settles onto the tangent direction.

07Differentiation rules

Theorem (Stewart §13.2, Theorem 3)

Let be differentiable vector functions, let , and let be a function.

  6.     [the Chain Rule]
Explanation (added)

Rules 3, 4 and 5 are all product rules — one for each kind of product a vector can take part in (scalar function times vector, dot, cross). They have the same shape: derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second. In rule 5 the order must be kept, because the cross product is not commutative (12.4).

What a typical exam question looks like
  • “Find the limit” of a vector function (watch for a component such as that needs a known limit), or “find the domain”.
  • “Sketch the curve with the given vector equation; indicate with an arrow the direction in which increases” — lines, segments, helices. The typed note in these notes says to practise the sketches for the first midterm.
  • “Find a vector function that represents the curve of intersection of the two surfaces” (a cylinder and a plane, as in the example).
  • “Find ” and “find the unit tangent vector at the given value of ”.
  • “Find parametric equations for the tangent line to the curve at the given point.”
